evidence.quote: The spacecraft is intended to image and send data to ground stations for collation and analysis.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.
Thus, only one satellite is required.

criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef/ocean monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users (operator/customers) are all covered with literature references. Some referencing is weak (Wikipedia used for launch data), but overall detailed and persuasive.

evidence.quote: Specifically, an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous.
An average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved
The proposed ZYZZsat is small and without thrusters in a low-earth orbit.

criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle, orbit elements, ground station, comms frequency, duration and EOL are addressed with STK evidence. But design has inconsistencies: no comms frequency/link budget, no coverage/swath analysis, EOL drag sail contradicts 'no thrusters' and no manoeuvre quantified, and launch rationale relies on Wikipedia. Adequate but not comprehensive.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.
The Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is well-located to receive data from this orbit type constantly and for long durations.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions summarise the design and acknowledge the unbuilt Vega E risk, but are largely generic restatements without quantified outcomes or critical assessment of limitations.

Structure with headings and executive summary is present, but figures are unnumbered/unlabelled (only captions), tables lack titles, references are bare URLs with no author/title/date, Wikipedia is cited, and there are typos ('purposed', 'complied'). Readable but not professional.

technical_issues.issue: RAAN 27.33° is stated to indicate launch facility location, which is incorrect; RAAN is set by launch time/azimuth, not site longitude.
No coverage/swath or resolution calculation to justify 600 km altitude; claim that high altitude gives low resolution is stated but not quantified.
No communication frequency band, data rate or link budget given, despite requirement to state comms frequency.
EOL drag sail described but no deorbit time/altitude analysis; text says satellite has no thrusters yet earlier mentions retro-burn options inconsistently.
Launch vehicle selection relies on Wikipedia '2021 in spaceflight' and an unbuilt Vega E; no delta-V or launch azimuth analysis.
Access table shows duplicate access 14/15 and a 151 s minimum pass; no assessment of data volume vs contact time.

overall: A competent, well-structured preliminary design covering most requirements with STK evidence, but weakened by missing comms frequency/link budget, no coverage analysis, questionable RAAN rationale, unlabelled figures, poor referencing (Wikipedia) and an under-supported EOL plan. Adequate overall.
